Subject: 4 stars - my game exists because of Murmur, but read this before you buy

I've used Murmur since August 2022. It's the nicest dialogue tool I've worked with, and right now it also has a serious problem, so this review is a bit of both.

The warning first, because that matters most if you're about to buy.

3.2.0 has a real bug. When you load a save that was made in 3.1.x, every Murmur variable is back to its default. In our game that means the ferryman forgets you already paid him. My guess is the save key changed from node path to a uid, but that is only a guess. Saves from 3.1.x are the case I can confirm.

Rolling back fixed it for us, and another dev in the forum confirmed the same:

1. Get the 3.1.4 release.
2. Replace the Murmur folder in your project's addons folder with it.
3. Keep a copy of 3.1.4 somewhere safe and don't update to 3.2.

After that our old saves loaded fine again. The forum thread is called "3.2.0: variables reset to default after loading a save" if you want the details.

The other thing you need to know is that there is no support anymore. Ines posted on 30 October that she is stepping back and that 3.2 is the last version she will make. So nobody is coming to fix this for you. If that's a dealbreaker for your project, that's fair, don't buy it. It's the reason this is 4 stars and not 5.

Now the other side.

The first prototype of Lanternfolk was literally one scene, the ferryman, and I made it in one weekend with Murmur in 2022. That was when I quit my job at a mobile studio. Today the game has 412 dialogue nodes in 9 languages, all of it going through Murmur's CSV export, and it comes out in December running on 3.1.4. I'm not a programmer who could have built a dialogue system like this on my own. Without this plugin there would be no game.

I paid 19 dollars for it. For that I got four years of updates, from 1.3 all the way to 3.2. So when I read here that she "took our money and ran" and "clearly doesn't care about customers", sorry, but that is just cruel. Be angry about the bug, that's fine, it's a bad bug. But one broken release at the end doesn't erase four years of work that a lot of us built our games on. She also said sorry for it herself in the pinned post, and nobody made her do that.

And the plugin isn't dead. The source is on the public repo under MIT now, so anyone can fork it and fix the save bug. Maybe someone will. Maybe even me once Lanternfolk is out, no promises.

So, for new people: 3.1.4 is solid and I'm shipping a whole game on it. 3.2 is broken for old saves and there's no support. Go in knowing that and you won't get burned.

And Ines, thank you. Lanternfolk wouldn't exist without your tool.
